_comment: Pinned source of truth for every mod on the Valheim estate. The server install, Mike's client, and the published client modpack are all generated from or checked against this file. Edit it FIRST, then deploy; never the other way round.
_versions: `version` is what Thunderstore calls the release and is what the modpack pins. `plugin_name` and `plugin_version` are what BepInEx prints in LogOutput.log, which is what scripts/mods-verify.mts compares against. They differ: the loader is packaged as 5.4.2350 and logs 5.4.23.5. A null plugin_name means the entry cannot be verified from the log, and the verifier reports that rather than passing it.

modpack.name: Utgarde_Client_Pack
modpack.description: Client mods for the Utgarde Valheim server, pinned to the versions the server runs.

server.method: scripts/mods-verify.mts against BepInEx/LogOutput.log after installing OdinOnDemand 1.2.5, OOD_LIB 1.2.0 and JsonDotNET 13.0.4; CLEAN at 21, up from 19, with OdinOnDemand 1.2.5 and Newtonsoft.Json Detector 1.0.0 the added rows and OOD_LIB reported as a LIBRARY that the log cannot carry. The log was truncated immediately before the restart so it covers this boot only, and fetched whole as gzip plus base64 over SSM with sha256 00108f6c6a2c56e81c357ae91cad27fbc1e8d7bbb50020af334a300569ccad3a matching on both ends. World load confirmed separately: Game server connected 05:56:06, Zonesystem Awake 05:56:07, DungeonDB Start 05:56:13. A world snapshot was taken with the server STOPPED, before the install, at /home/steam/world-snapshots/Utgarde.pre-ood-20260922T055425Z, 221 files against 221 in the source, with the install gated on that count matching.
server.errors: 13 '[Error' lines and zero 'Exception' lines this boot, against a control of 463 log lines, and a set difference against the PRE-OdinOnDemand boot of the same day is empty, so the three new packages introduced no new error kind. All 13 are the vanilla headless noise already documented: AsyncResourceUpload, missing video decode shaders, the intro cinematic. Warnings actually FELL from 13 to 11.
server.odinondemand_on_linux: The win-x64 LibVLC runtime was the open question and it is answered: 48 files and 31 MB of Windows natives sit in plugins/libvlc on a Linux box and nothing tried to touch them. A whole-word grep for vlc, libvlc and LibVLCSharp across the boot returns NOTHING, so no VLC initialisation was attempted and none failed. OdinOnDemand's own logger printed one line, its load line, which on its own would be weak evidence. The stronger evidence is that it created BepInEx/config/OdinOnDemand/ at 05:55 holding four files, including recipes.json and recipes_item.json: a mod that has written out the recipes for its own buildable pieces has run well past construction. Contrast ForsakenShrines in the same boot, which narrates every prefab it clones; OdinOnDemand is simply a quiet mod.
server.unverified: TWO items, neither covered by the CLEAN. First, unchanged from the previous entry: PortalProgression's GATING, which needs a player to carry ore through a portal. Second, new: whether OdinOnDemand's media players REGISTER as build pieces server-side and SURVIVE. The log does not say, the roster was 0 throughout, and the failure mode if they do not is the one ForsakenShrines already documents here: a server that cannot resolve a prefab deletes its ZDO rather than ignoring it. Settle it before anyone builds anything expensive: place one media player, relog, and confirm it is still there.

client_jetragon.method: hand install into the Gale Default profile, every DLL hash-compared against the downloaded artifact; GentleDeath, AdventureBackpacks and VikingsDoSwim exercised in game
client_jetragon.stale: STALE as of pack 1.14.0 (2026-09-22). The 2026-09-15 hand check predates every mod added since, and OdinOnDemand is now a third enforced mod alongside ValheimPlus and AdventureBackpacks, so an un-updated client is refused at connect rather than degraded. jetragon needs pack 1.14.0 plus the hand-installed Animal Feeding Trough 1.0.3, and, for OdinOnDemand specifically, a JavaScript runtime beside yt-dlp for full YouTube quality and Streamlink for Twitch or Kick. Neither of those two blocks connecting.

pack.method: scripts/modpack-publish.mts. Its readback guard fired on submit again, reporting the version absent with HTTP 404 despite a 2xx, so presence was polled separately rather than inferred: Thunderstore reports valheimsquad-Utgarde_Client_Pack-1.14.0 is_active with 22 dependencies, and OdinOnDemand, OOD_LIB and JsonDotNET were each checked present BY NAME rather than taken from the count going up. The build confirmed all 22 pinned versions exist upstream before writing.
pack.window: The server gained OdinOnDemand at 05:56:06 and the pack was live at 06:01, about five minutes in which the box carried an enforced mod the published pack did not. The roster read 0 before the stop and the deploy gate aborts on any non-zero or unreadable count, so nobody was connected to be dropped. Second such window in an hour after the 1.13.0 one at 04:55; both are unavoidable given the box has to be proven before the pack is published, and both were kept to single-digit minutes at zero players.

mods.why: The BepInEx loader itself. Everything below is inert without it.
Craft-from-chest, map sharing, smelter tuning, build and taming settings. The server sets enforceMod = true, so a client on any other version is kicked at connect.
mods.note: 10.2.0 is the Valheim 1.0.15 compatibility release, published 2026-09-19, the day after the game build moved. The 10.1.2 it replaces shipped 2026-09-14 and predates the patch, so the estate ran a pre-patch V+ on a post-patch server for four days. Two behaviour changes ship with it and NEITHER bites this box, both read off the regenerated config on 2026-09-22. difficultyScaleRange defaulted to 2 metres whenever the Game section was enabled, which was a bug, and now defaults to 100; here [Game] carries enabled = false, so the 200 set in that section is inert and always was. Oven settings now affect only the oven rather than every fuel-burning cooking station. The new [FrigidKiln] and [FrostFoundry] sections for the 1.0.15 Deep North stations were written into the config at lines 912 and 957, which is independent evidence the new DLL generated it rather than inheriting the old one. enforceMod = true at line 2041, so the client pack has to match this pin exactly.

mods.why: Mod library. Server-side it backs ServersideQoL; client-side it is required by Animal Feeding Trough and, since pack 1.10.0, by Muted_Mist.
mods.note: AdventureBackpacks pins this exactly, so the two move together or not at all, and the floor has now moved three times inside this estate's life: 2.26.1, then 2.30.1, now 2.30.2. The zip uses Windows path separators: unzip normalises them, a plain Python extractall does not. 2.30.2 fixes Deep North assets overriding vanilla ones and the legacy build menu breaking under 2.30.1's category changes.

mods.why: Berry bushes, thistle, dandelions, mushrooms and several trees on the cultivator. Degrades rather than blocking: a client without it still sees what others plant.
ServersideQoL dependency server-side; AdventureBackpacks declares it client-side too, so every player now carries it.

Framework the three ServersideQoL modules below plug into. 2.0.4 silently stopped on the 1.0.12 network-version bump and took PortalProgression down with it, so this pin is load-bearing after every game patch.
mods.note: Ships TWO artifacts and they must move together: plugins/ServersideQoL.dll and patchers/ServersideQoL.Patchers.dll, which BepInEx loads first and which patches assembly_valheim. Upgrading only the plugin leaves the patcher a version behind, and the load log reports both, so check the 'Loaded 1 patcher method from [ServersideQoL.Patchers ...]' line as well as the plugin line. 2.0.14 turns config auto-reload on by default and fixes occasional item loss when a module modifies a container on a non-dedicated server.

mods.why: Boss-gated ore through portals. The group voted for progression gating over free teleporting.
mods.note: 2.0.11 is this module's latest and it declares a hard dependency on ServersideQoL 2.0.11, while the core here runs 2.0.14. That mismatch is normal for this author, who releases the core more often than the modules, and the estate has run a newer core under a 2.0.11 module since 2026-09-18 with the load log clean. The pin is Thunderstore's resolver, not a runtime check. Verify this module by BEHAVIOUR after any core bump rather than by its load line: it is the module that logged a clean load and silently stopped gating ore on the 1.0.12 network bump, which is the incident the whole verification habit exists for.

mods.why: Auto-sort, auto-pickup, and stack-into-nearby-chests on the Cheer emote.
Content signs on chests, and how a chest is designated for other ServersideQoL modules.
mods.note: 2.0.11 moved two settings out of this mod: AutoPickupMaxRange went to AutoStore and FeedFromContainersMaxRange went to AutoProcess, which this estate does not install. Both were sitting at the default of 64 here, so nothing needed re-homing, but a future custom value set on the wrong side of that split goes silently inert.

mods.name: Animal Feeding Trough
mods.why: Boss-free feeding for tamed animals. Clients MUST have it: the server rejects a connection with "Missing mods: Animal Feeding Trough 1.0.3", observed 2026-09-12. It is Nexus-only, so the pack cannot carry it and every player installs it by hand. Replace it with a Thunderstore equivalent when a maintained one appears; the AutoFeed family is the closest, but every candidate wants an older Jotunn or BepInEx than this estate runs.

Valheim 1.0 blocks Steam achievements for anyone running mods, so this pack is what disables them. Unshamed restores them and returns the ones already earned, granting no free unlocks. It is here because the pack causes the problem it fixes. Client-only: achievements are a Steam client concern and the server has no use for it.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Saves the server password and adds a quick-connect button for the last server, so nobody retypes it every session. Chosen over Dedryx-QuickServerConnect because it covers both jobs in one mod: two mods hooking the same join dialog and both storing passwords is a conflict waiting to happen. Client-only and purely convenience, so dropping it breaks nothing. Published 2026-09-12 and therefore unproven here; remove it if it misbehaves.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Craftable, wearable backpacks with tiers. Replaces ArgusMagnus-ServersideQoL_Backpack, which was server-only and therefore cheaper to deploy, but was an invisible container opened by an emote rather than an item in the world. Since the pack reaches every player anyway, the deployment saving bought nothing. Jotunn-based, so a client without it is kicked at connect exactly like ValheimPlus.
mods.note: Ships a Translations/ folder beside the DLL; 15 json files, copied on both sides. 2.1.10 hard-requires Jotunn 2.30.2, so the two can never be bumped independently: the floor was 2.26.1 at 2.0.4 and 2.30.1 at 2.0.9. Two fixes in this range earn the jump on this estate specifically. 2.1.9 fixes dedicated servers failing to load backpacks while waiting on a user-interface event, which is a server-side fault this box was exposed to. 2.1.9 also fixes cold effects bleeding through when a weather mod is running, naming Seasonality, which this estate runs with every season set to two days, so winter arrives often.
mods.telemetry: 2.0.6 added anonymous telemetry its changelog described as defaulting to enabled with auto-opt-in on launch. 2.0.9 REVERSED that, and 2.1.10 holds the line: read off the box's regenerated config on 2026-09-22, 'Enable Anonymous Telemetry' under [Local Config] is false and marked [Not Synced with Server], so the server cannot set it for players either way. That is a re-read at 2.1.10, not the 2.0.9 reading carried forward. The same section carries 'Show Splash on Startup = true', also client-local, so players see a splash on first launch after updating.

mods.why: Keeps equipables (weapons, armor, tools, shields, ammo, utility, trinkets) on death and sends everything else to the tombstone, classifying via Valheim's own ItemData.IsEquipable(). Replaces beefbaccio-DeathTweaks, which shipped in pack 1.3.0 and coincided with every player stuck at 1 health; that attribution was never proven, but DeathTweaks predated Valheim 1.0 and this one declares 1.0.x compatibility. Verified working on jetragon 2026-09-15.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.note: 1.0.13 is a readme change and nothing else, per the author's own changelog. Taken so the pin stays current rather than for any behaviour, and the DLL hash did move, so it was rebuilt.

mods.why: Scales swim speed, stamina regen and stamina drain to the Swim skill, and adds diving. Vanilla swimming was the complaint. Verified on jetragon 2026-09-15.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Ground transport: a tameable, rideable, breedable horse with armour and an attachable cart. Added 2026-09-18 because overland travel to the traders and back is the group's standing complaint, and vanilla offers nothing below the Plains lox saddle. Chosen on maintenance rather than features: it is the only mod in this category still shipping, updated 2026-09-15, against a field where the nearest alternatives (BeastsOfBurden 2021, CraftyCartsRemake and ValheimRAFT early 2026) are stale. Declares no dependencies and bundles its assets in a 10.5 MB DLL, so it needs nothing else on the box. Config syncs from the server like ValheimPlus.
mods.note: Whether it rejects a client that lacks it is UNVERIFIED. It is not Jotunn-based, so the mod-enforcement path that kicks a client missing AdventureBackpacks or the trough does not apply, but it does add prefabs and a client without them is untested. Shipping it in the pack in the same pass as the server install is what keeps that question academic. Its own readme opens by telling you to back up character and world files before installing or updating. 1.7.1 through 1.7.3 are a piecemanager bump and added localisations, with no behaviour change the changelog names.

mods.why: Seasonal textures and colours, plus weather. Chosen over shudnal-Seasons because that one carries gameplay effects on crops and water, and we had just finished tuning crop growth. Modifiers Enabled ships Off and every per-season stat multiplier is 1, so out of the box it is purely visual, which is what was asked for. Depends on YamlDotNet, already carried for AdventureBackpacks.
mods.why_server_side: Client-only was tried first, on the reasoning that the season derives from world age so clients would agree without server sync. Measured 2026-09-18: seasons never advanced, sitting on the configured Summer for days while the client logged a healthy load. Installed server-side the same night, after which the server logs 'Seasonal Timer Awake'. The mod's README lists season_winter and siblings as GLOBAL KEYS, which only a server writes, and every config entry is marked [Synced with Server] with the in-game set command admin-only. Those point the same way but do not by themselves prove the old reasoning wrong; the proof is a season actually flipping, which had not yet happened when this was written.
mods.note: Ships a config/Seasonality texture tree alongside the DLL; a mod manager places it, a hand install must copy it into BepInEx/config. Season lengths live in the server's copy of the config as a Vector3 of days, hours, minutes, with 30 real minutes to the in-game day. All four are set to two days, against a stock default of five in-game hours that cycles a whole year every 25 real minutes. 3.8.3 adds a Warm_Twilight_SnowStorm environment because vanilla's Twilight_SnowStorm became freezing in Valheim 1.0, and instructs you to reset configs or change winter weather by hand. Checked against this estate's config on 2026-09-18 and it does NOT apply: Twilight_SnowStorm appears nowhere here, every [Winter] weather list already reads WarmSnow:1,Twilight_Snow:0.5,WarmSnowStorm:0.1, and Always Cold and Wet Freezes are both Off. Re-check that grep rather than the changelog if the warning resurfaces.

mods.why: Browser map of the live world, served from the box over the Cloudflare tunnel, showing the terrain every player has explored plus player pins and pin sharing. Server-side only: it renders from the world the server holds, so clients install nothing. Chosen over Mubs-WebMap and the other h0tw1r3 forks because it is the one still shipping, and because it keeps the 3D view and renders history rather than only what is explored while it runs.
mods.note: Ships a web/ tree beside the DLL and writes rendered tiles into plugins/WebMap/map_data, which reached 110 MB on first full reveal, so it is not a candidate for the backup set. Its zip uses Windows path separators, so a plain extractall produces files literally named 'plugins\WebMap\web\js\app.js'; normalise the separators on extract. The three h0tw1r3 forks share the config filename com.github.h0tw1r3.valheim.webmap.cfg, so a fork swap that leaves the old file behind silently inherits the previous fork's values.

mods.why: The visual upgrade the group asked for. Explicitly NOT a ReShade-style screen filter: its effects hook Valheim's own lighting, water, weather, biome and time-of-day systems, so they respond to the world rather than tinting the frame. Ships wind-driven cloud shadows, underwater caustics and Meadows fireflies on by default. Chosen over the texture-replacement mods because those are limited to vegetation and their own author recommends this one instead.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.note: Requires Direct3D 11; its readme states Vulkan is not currently validated, so a client launching with -force-vulkan may misbehave. Windows only. Declares no Jotunn dependency and no network sync. More usefully than that reasoning, it was OBSERVED on 2026-09-19 that a client lacking this batch's mods connected and spawned normally (05:40:44Z), and neither new server-side DLL carries a Jotunn NetworkCompatibility string, so nothing here enforces a version match. Its own readme says do NOT install it on a dedicated server; it has no server-side behaviour. The Enhanced Environment colour-grading feature ships Enabled = false and was deliberately left off: it is the one opinionated feature and visibly recolours the game. 0.5.15 through 0.5.17 tune the three features that ship on by default: cloud shadows now form in broad bands rather than one uniform dapple size, the finest shadow octave is dropped when the mask cannot resolve it, which removes shimmer at high ShadowDrawDistance, and underwater caustics now fall off on vertical faces instead of lighting walls like floors. Its zip uses Windows path separators, the same trap as Jotunn's.

mods.why: Grass density and draw distance, so clutter stops popping in a few metres ahead of the player. Chosen on currency rather than popularity: ShadowField-GrassTweaks has ten times the downloads and is recommended by other mods' readmes, but was last updated 2025-07-26, before Valheim 1.0. This one was updated 2026-09-14 and declares no dependencies at all. Its own readme nonetheless says 'Built for Valheim 1.0.12', three patches behind this estate's 1.0.15, which is a real qualification on the currency argument above: recent upload date and declared target build are different things, and none of the three drift checks compares the latter against game_version.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Rendering and loading optimisations, taken to buy frame headroom for the draw distance and effects the rest of this batch adds rather than to fix a performance problem. Declares no dependencies.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.why_not_server_side: The package advertises itself as working on servers, but its author's own readme says 'I have not tested this mod on servers'. It also ships Unity.Burst.dll, Unity.Burst.Unsafe.dll and Unity.Mathematics.dll into the GAME's Managed directory rather than into BepInEx/plugins, and this box re-runs SteamCMD on boot, which owns that directory. Almost every optimisation it lists is rendering work a headless server never does: light flicker culling, reflection probes, particle culling, audiosource culling. Only the ZDO ownership scan is server-relevant. Untested-by-author plus writing into a SteamCMD-managed directory, for one server-side win, is a poor trade on a live world.
mods.artifact_sha256_note: Six of the seven binaries this package ships. The seventh, VPOBurst_linux_x86_64.so, was not hashed because the download sweep matched *.dll only; it is irrelevant here in any case, since this mod is client-only and the clients are Windows. The three Unity DLLs are recorded specifically because they land in the game's Managed directory rather than BepInEx/plugins.

mods.why: Draw distance: controls how far zones are rendered, loaded and generated. Its readme says to install it on the server and optionally on clients, so the server copy is what the client's own limits are raised against; whether extended limits are strictly impossible without it is untested here. This is a maintained fork of JereKuusela's Render Limits, rebuilt and smoke-tested against Valheim 1.0.14 at network version 40. The network version matches this estate; the game version does not, since this estate runs 1.0.15. and it preserves the original render_limits plugin GUID and config keys.
mods.note: Installed at stock values. 1.16.0 specifically added server-side guardrails against a client requesting an excessive loaded radius, plus a 'Maximum force active zones' bound, so raising limits is a deliberate follow-up rather than something to crank blind. Each zone is 64x64 m.

mods.why: Thins the Mistlands mist instead of deleting it. One setting, TransparencyIntensity, where 0 hides the mist entirely and 1 is vanilla; the estate runs 0.7, a gentle trim. Chosen over Vapok-NoFogBruh, which removes fog outright and was rejected as effectively cheating in the Mistlands, and over ComfyMods-Dramamist, which does the same job but predates Valheim 1.0.
mods.note: Config changes take effect LIVE, with no restart, which is unusual on this estate and makes it the cheapest setting here to tune in place. Installed server-side deliberately: its readme says a server install enforces the configuration on clients, and leaving it off the server would let each player choose, but it is the only mod in this batch that declares a Jotunn dependency, which is the one kick path this estate has actually seen fire. That made it the likeliest to enforce a version match, not the only thing that conceivably could; it was afterwards observed not to enforce one. One shared value is the cheaper trade. Its shipped default is TransparencyIntensity = 0.2, which is near-invisible mist, NOT vanilla; 0.7 here is therefore a raise off the default rather than a cut from vanilla. Read the generated config before assuming a mod's default is the vanilla behaviour.

mods.why: Replants a sapling where a felled tree's stump is destroyed, so logging does not permanently strip the map. Requested by the operator 2026-09-19; no reason beyond the request was given. Chosen as the only maintained member of its family: it is a rebuild of Aedenthorn's TreeRespawn, and of the surviving forks of that original the freshest is Lyric-TreeRespawn_by_Aedenthorn 0.8.5, last updated 2026-03-10, with most of the rest deprecated, against this one's 2026-09-11. Its readme declares the target as "Updated for Valheim 1.0" with no patch number, so the fourth drift check is INDETERMINATE here rather than clean: unlike WiresGrassTweaks there is no number to compare against game_version 1.0.15. Sole declared dependency is BepInExPack 5.4.2202, older than the 5.4.2350 this estate runs.
mods.note: Ships a plugins/configs/ tree beside the DLL, so a hand install must copy the folder and not just the DLL; same trap as Seasonality's config tree and AdventureBackpacks' Translations folder. ALL FOUR dictionaries must be present, because the mod picks one at RUNTIME by probing BepInEx for a planting mod's GUID: advize.PlantEverything selects tree_dict_Plant_Everything.json, com.Defryder.Plant_all_trees selects tree_dict_Plant_all_trees.json, com.bkeyes93.PlantingPlus selects tree_dict_PlantingPlus.json, and tree_dict.json is the fallback when none is loaded. This estate runs Advize-PlantEverything, so it resolves to the PlantEverything dictionary with no configuration, and that dictionary differs: it maps SwampTree1_Stub to Ancient_Sapling where the fallback maps SwampTree1 to SwampTree1. Shipping only tree_dict.json would leave the selected file missing, which is a silent failure. The mod prints "Loaded <n> seeds from <file>" on startup, so the chosen dictionary is verifiable from the server log rather than inferred. Config keys live under [General]: Enabled, RespawnDelay, treeRate, useRandomSapling, checkcraftingtable, noswamptreerespawn, GrowthSpaceRestriction, DebugMode.
mods.sync: Bundles ServerSync inside the DLL rather than declaring it as a dependency, so the server holds the config and locks it to clients. The DLL's own text says "It's required that the mod is installed on the server and all clients" and carries ServerSync's version-mismatch path ("Received server version is not equal"), so treat this as a mod that can refuse a mismatched client and keep the deploy-to-publish window short. ServerSync is not Jotunn's ModCompatibility, and whether a client lacking the mod is actually refused here is UNVERIFIED; the author's statement and the version check are the evidence, not an observation.

mods.why: Buildable shrines, one per defeated Forsaken, that channel that boss's guardian power once its trophy is mounted, so swapping a power costs a build instead of a run to the world-centre stones. Picked by the operator 2026-09-19 over turbero-ForsakenPowersPlusRemastered 2.0.4, which does the same job with an F8 hotkey. THE DECIDING AXIS WAS DESIGN, NOT PACKAGE HEALTH: a hotkey deletes the trip, while a shrine keeps the mechanic and puts a price on it, one build plus consumed trophies per boss. That is the same rule that put ServersideQoL_PortalProgression here instead of free portals, Muted_Mist instead of NoFogBruh, and GentleDeath instead of DeathTweaks: gate the mechanic, do not remove it. Depends on Jotunn 2.30.0, under the 2.30.1 already here, and on BepInExPack 5.4.2350, which matches exactly.
mods.risk: MAINTENANCE risk only, which is a separate axis from the design choice in `why` and does not qualify it. The author labels 0.8.3 ALPHA in his own readme, and it had 257 downloads at install time against the alternative's 3448, so upstream may move or stall under us. On the fourth drift it is the WIDEST gap recorded here: the readme says "Built against Valheim 1.0.7" against game_version 1.0.15, eight patches, where Wire-WiresGrassTweaks' 1.0.12 was three. None of the three drift checks can see any of that, so re-read the readme's declared target on every upgrade. The package also carries Thunderstore's AI Generated tag; recorded as a fact about the listing, explicitly NOT as a concern, because the operator has ruled that out of scope for this estate.
mods.note: UNINSTALLING THIS SERVER-SIDE PERMANENTLY DESTROYS EVERY SHRINE PLAYERS HAVE BUILT. The shrines are new prefabs, and Valheim deletes ZDOs it cannot instantiate, silently and with no recovery. That is not a hypothetical: the mod's own 0.8.3 changelog is describing what already happened to its users, because 0.8.2 and earlier carried [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")], which makes BepInEx skip the plugin entirely under valheim_server.exe, so it could not load on a dedicated server at all. Treat removal as a destructive operation needing a world backup, never as a rollback. The same reasoning is why it is side 'both' rather than client-only. Version enforcement is ServerSync's, not Jotunn's ModCompatibility: the DLL declares no NetworkCompatibility attribute, and the disconnect path it does carry refuses a client whose ForsakenShrines version differs from the server's, while a client with the mod absent entirely can still connect. So the pack and the box must move together, but a player who never installs it is not locked out. Placement is constrained: natural terrain only, open sky above, and a Stonecutter in range; shrines sit in the vanilla stone hammer tab because Valheim 1.0 hard-limits build categories. Every setting except 'Mod Enabled' is server-synced; that one is client-local and needs a relaunch. 0.8.5 fixes one arm of that destruction: setting 'Mod Enabled = false' on a dedicated server used to skip prefab registration, so the server deleted every shrine ZDO it could not resolve. A dedicated server now ignores that setting, loads anyway, and logs why. The guidance above is unchanged and is now what upstream says too: take the mod off a server by removing the DLL, never by flipping the setting. 0.8.4 added a 'Lock Configuration' setting under General, on by default and held by the server.
mods.symptom_to_remember: Spinning camera plus a character frozen in the wake-up pose on login, on Valheim 1.0, means SOME installed mod is registering build pieces through Jotunn's PieceManager, whose patch targets a field Valheim 1.0 removed; it throws every physics tick and aborts player spawning whenever a Hammer is equipped. It is not specific to this mod. ForsakenShrines 0.8.1 did it, 0.8.2 stopped using PieceManager, and Jotunn 2.30.0 fixes it for mods that still do. Worth knowing before that symptom gets chased as a graphics or client problem.
mods.config_state: Read on the box 2026-09-22 after the 0.8.5 install: 'Mod Enabled = true' and the new 'Lock Configuration = true' that 0.8.4 added, which is its shipped default and holds the synced config against client edits.

mods.why: Newtonsoft.Json, packaged for Valheim by the ValheimModding team. Carried only because OdinOnDemand declares it. Nothing else on the estate asks for it.
mods.note: The shim logs 'Newtonsoft.Json Detector 1.0.0' while the package is versioned 13.0.4, the same split the YamlDotNet shim has. Read off the box 2026-09-22 after a guess of 'Newtonsoft Json Detector' was wrong by one dot. Worth knowing: on this server it does not load anything. Its own line reads 'Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.0.0 assembly already loaded from valheim_server_Data/Managed/Newtonsoft.Json.dll', because the game itself ships Newtonsoft at that path. Detecting that and standing down is the shim's whole job, so it is doing it. The package is carried because OdinOnDemand declares it, not because the server needs it.

mods.why: OdinOnDemand's support libraries, declared as a hard dependency. Seven managed DLLs that resolve media URLs: YoutubeExplode, YoutubeDLSharp, SoundCloudExplode and four System/Bcl shims. No native code, so it is platform-neutral and safe on the Linux box.
mods.plugin_name_note: Seven plain assemblies and no BepInEx plugin, so it cannot appear in a load log on either side. Verified by file presence instead: the deploy hash-checks YoutubeExplode.dll, YoutubeDLSharp.dll and SoundCloudExplode.dll against this entry before installing, and confirms 3/3 on the box afterwards. Do not reach for the transitive argument that OdinOnDemand loading proves these are present: OdinOnDemand may only touch them on a playback path a dedicated server never takes, so its load line says nothing about them.

mods.why: Cinema screens, televisions and music players built in world, playing YouTube, SoundCloud, Twitch, Kick and direct HTTP(S) streams for everyone in earshot. Asked for by the operator 2026-09-22. 1.2 rebuilt it on LibVLC and restored its own build-menu category on Valheim 1.0's new system.
mods.enforcement: Jotunn NetworkCompatibility, confirmed by reading the strings in OdinOnDemand.dll rather than inferred from it being Jotunn-based: the assembly carries both NetworkCompatibilityAttribute and VersionStrictness. That is the same kick path that already fires for AdventureBackpacks, so the box and the published pack must move together and a player on the old pack is refused at connect.
mods.why_linux_is_fine: The package is 24.8 MB and most of it is a win-x64 LibVLC runtime, which cannot execute on this Linux box. It still loads, for reasons that were CHECKED rather than assumed. The assembly carries no BepInProcess attribute and names neither valheim.exe nor valheim_server.exe, so BepInEx does not skip it under valheim_server.exe; that is the exact way ForsakenShrines 0.8.2 failed here, so it was the first thing looked for. It does carry IsDedicated, IsServer and ZNet, so a server branch exists in the code. The readme scopes the VLC runtime to 'every client' and describes the server's job as simulating station playback position and sending it to players, which is bookkeeping rather than decoding. The libvlc tree is installed on the server anyway, inert, because the readme also says clients and servers must have identical files and 40 MB of dormant Windows DLLs is the cheaper risk.
mods.player_setup: Two capabilities need an executable the Thunderstore pack CANNOT ship, so they are per-player hand installs like Animal Feeding Trough. Neither blocks connecting. YouTube works without them but the readme warns quality or audio availability may be limited without a JavaScript runtime beside yt-dlp: Deno 2.3+, Node, Bun or QuickJS, and Proton needs the Windows x64 deno.exe. Twitch and Kick need Streamlink on every client that wants to watch them. Direct HTTP(S) audio and video, radio stations and SoundCloud need nothing extra, because the bundled VLC handles them.
mods.drift_target_build: INDETERMINATE, the same verdict TreesReborn carries. The readme says 'updated for Valheim 1.0' and 'Valheim 1.0 support' with no patch number, so there is nothing to compare against game_version 1.0.15. Worth watching: 1.2.5 shipped 2026-09-15 and the game moved to 1.0.15 on 2026-09-18, so this is the one mod on the estate whose latest release predates the current game build.
mods.note: Config lives in BepInEx/config/OdinOnDemand/ rather than a single cfg file. The readme lists admin-only settings, a VIP mode and remote-control options, none of which are configured yet.

mods.why: Admin console tooling: enables devcommands and the admin utilities around them on a dedicated server, which vanilla refuses to a remote admin. Installed on the box by hand on 2026-09-20 at 19:45 UTC and found by scripts/mods-verify.mts on 2026-09-22, which reported it UNEXPECTED because no record mentioned it.
mods.why_not_in_pack: Operator tooling, like the ConfigurationManager entry below. It grants console powers that are admin-gated anyway, so shipping it to five players installs something none of them can use. Recorded here rather than left out, because an absent entry reads as an oversight and the verifier will flag it as drift on every run until it is written down.
mods.note: Already at its own latest, 1.113.0, so it is not part of this pass's nine. Its sole declared dependency is BepInExPack 5.4.2350, which matches the loader here exactly. It lives in its own plugins/JereKuusela-Server_devcommands/ directory rather than loose in plugins/, which is why a directory listing alone does not make it obvious.

mods.why: In-game editor for every BepInEx setting, opened with F1. It is how the admin changes a [Synced with Server] value without a config edit and a server restart, which is the difference between turning the rain off in ten seconds and bouncing everyone. Added 2026-09-20, when Seasonality's weather lists needed changing mid-session and there was no way to do it from inside the game.
mods.why_not_in_pack: Operator tooling, not something the group plays with. It edits settings that are admin-only to change anyway, so shipping it to every player installs a GUI five people cannot use to change anything. Kept in this manifest rather than left out, because an absent entry reads as an oversight and invites the next session to add it to the pack; admin_only is the recorded decision not to.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
